**`packages/spec/src/system/tracing.test.ts:545`**

> `it('leaves the OTel exporter \`timeout\` alone — its describe names no unit, so it is outside the population', () => { … expect(config.exporter.timeout).toBe(10000); })`

That is this card's row `:541`. **This card is the sweep that guard was written to catch, so the guard succeeds by failing.** Its whole title — the key name, "names no unit", and "outside the population" — goes false when this card lands.

⛔ It is not to be deleted, `.skip`ped, weakened, or "fixed green". It is to be replaced by a refusal pin (the issue is **not** `unrecognized_keys`, and the message carries the FROM → TO mapping), an acceptance pin at the same magnitude (10000) with the same default, and a describe pin asserting the unit is now published — and relocated if its enclosing `describe` header would otherwise become false. That is the shape PR #17983 used for the identical situation on `plugin-security-advanced.test.ts:401`, and PR #17986 for `plugin-lifecycle-advanced`.

Two things to carry into the same round:

- Re-run the sweep across `packages/spec/src` for the other three rows (`exportTimeout`, `scheduledDelay`, `exportInterval`) — a green `check:duration-unit-keys` cannot see a stale sentence, only a stale describe.
- Note that `tracing.test.ts:537` already carries a landed `Span.duration → durationMs` retirement with exactly the refusal shape to copy from, on this same file.

The full dispatch order follows when the card is claimed.

`#15679` already renamed `Span.duration → durationMs` on **this same file** — it is the one already-suffixed key-position declaration on it. ⚠️ One judgement to show your work on: `exporter.timeout` and `exporter.batch.exportTimeout` would become `timeoutMs` and `exportTimeoutMs` — two `*TimeoutMs` keys one nesting level apart. Check that reads unambiguously and say why you accepted or rejected it.

### 2.4 Tombstones, and the TDZ ordering trap

Check `.strict()` on each enclosing object. Where absent, a bare deletion is an **ADR-0049 silent strip** — the operator's value vanishes and a default lands on an exporter deadline. Every row needs a `retiredKey()` tombstone whose message carries the FROM → TO mapping.

Check where each new const has to sit.
